subject: known abundance in pcount / N-mixture models?

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: known abundance in pcount / N-mixture models?
parts:
Greetings all,

I'm interested in the detection process underlying some count data and not in the abundance/state process. I've used an offset (log of known abundance) to predict abundance (and several highly predictive detection covariates), but I'm still getting unreasonably high estimates of abundance due to the intercept (I tried the NB mixture, but P was the most realistic). Is there a way to either (1) remove the intercept (attempted; consistently crashes R) or (2) assign a known abundance vector similar to knownOcc in an occu model?

Thanks, as always, to the unmarked developers and community!

Giancarlo

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] known abundance in pcount / N-mixture models?
parts:
hi Giancarlo,
 I don't think removing the intercept makes any sense in this case. I think estimates are probably unreasonably high because p is really low and the MLEs can be very unstable in that situation or there is over-dispersion not being modeled.
 Regarding (2) -- it would be possible to assign known abundance if you used a Bayesian analysis in BUGS or JAGs.  You could do this using likelihood methods but not as an option in unmarked.
regards
andy

parts:
Thanks Andy,

My (perhaps silly) thought in removing the intercept (estimate = 1.03) in this case was that the predicted abundance is equal to exp(1.03+ log(knownAbundance)) when log(knownAbundance) is used as an offset. I've attached two plots showing this.

In looking at naive estimates of detection (i.e., each survey's observed abundance / known abundance), the mean is 0.44, SD = 0.31.

Thanks again. -Giancarlo
